results.text:
Trigger: When finalizing a yes/no answer about whether a finding is visible in a named lung subregion after a grounded chest-imaging report, especially when one report phrase names a more specific location such as “apical” but another phrase or bounding box describes the same abnormality more broadly.

Observable verification action: Reopen the raw grounded report and its boxes, enumerate every positive finding for the same abnormality and lung, and check whether any stated finding or bounding box covers the queried subregion. Answer Yes if the report contains positive evidence of that abnormality within the queried region; do not answer No solely because the residual finding is described as “apical” or because the exact words “lower left” do not appear. If no positive evidence covers the queried subregion, answer No. If options are displayed, map the supported text back to the option letter and confirm they agree.

In this case, the original final answer relied on “small left apical pneumothorax remains” and inferred no lower-left pneumothorax, while overlooking “Left pneumothorax has been reduced” with a box extending into the lower left lung region. That was an evidence/conclusion failure, not an option-mapping error.

Trigger: Finalizing a left-versus-right lung abnormality answer after a grounded chest-imaging report, especially when the rationale cites a specific finding from that report.

Observable verification action: Reopen the raw grounded-report observation and locate the exact statement for each lung. Choose a side only if an explicit abnormal finding is attributed to that lung—for example, “3.2 cm nodular density in the left mid-lung”—and the opposite lung is explicitly clear or normal—for example, “the right lung is clear.” Do not treat a non-lung incidental finding such as a left-sided PICC line as proof of lung abnormality. If options are displayed, map the supported side text back to the displayed choice and confirm the letter and text agree; if options are empty, confirm the terminal answer text matches the supported side and that the cited phrase actually appears in the observed report.

Trigger: Finalizing a broad “Are there any abnormalities?” answer when one tool says “No” for a limited abnormality checklist but another tool reports positive findings.

Observable verification action: Enumerate every abnormal finding reported across tool observations and compare each negative answer with its exact scope. If the question asks broadly about any abnormality and any observation reports one—such as an atherosclerotic aorta, sternal suture fracture, or post-sternotomy change—answer Yes and cite that observed finding. Do not let a narrow “No” for consolidation/effusion/pneumothorax/cardiomegaly overrule a broader positive report. If choices are present, also map the supported answer text back to the displayed option and verify the letter and text agree.
